findings.title: Shared operator/join token is baked into public app release bundles
evidence: .github/workflows/build-app.yml:59-64 - build step sets env BENCH_BAKE_AGENT_CONF: ${{ secrets.BENCH_AGENT_CONF }}

packaging/build_app.py:66-84 - write_agent_conf() writes the secret content to <bundle>/bench-agent.conf; docstring line 70-72 admits CI passes the secret so a downloaded app auto-registers and the app releases are public (world-readable)
bench/benchreport.py:138-152 - the agent/GUI/TUI load (server, token) from <toolkit>/bench-agent.conf baked into the bundle
server/benchd.py:14-26 - the single BENCHD_TOKEN is BOTH the join/registration token AND the operator API bearer
README.md:158-163 - README instructs baking BENCH_AGENT_CONF into bundles and warns the token is world-readable
findings.impact: Anyone who downloads the public app release gets the control-plane token. In this app that token is the operator bearer (server/benchd.py:15,26), so it grants full control-plane access: registering runners, reading all run/telemetry data, and issuing privileged commands (update/exec/shell/reboot - benchd.py:1223-1225). The README's suggested mitigation ('use a limited, rotatable token') is unsupported by the code, which has no limited/runner-only registration token.
findings.recommendation: Do not bake a shared operator token into public artifacts. Introduce a distinct, runner-scoped bootstrap/registration token (accepted only by POST /api/v1/register, unable to act as operator), or have the bundle ship empty and prompt for config. If a token must ship, generate a per-build token and document its immediate revocation.

findings.title: Write-capable GitHub PAT is baked into the public live-USB ISO
evidence: .github/workflows/build-iso.yml:62-71 - CI writes secrets.BENCH_UPLOAD_CONF to live/private/bench-upload.conf
live/Build-LiveUSB.sh:127-132 - installs it as /etc/bench-upload.conf with mode 600 into the squashfs image
bench/upload.py:10-16 - config format documents GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_xxx with 'Contents: Read/Write'
README.md:357-363 and AGENTS.md:176-182 - state ISO releases are public downloads and the token is world-readable; rotate if a stick is shared
findings.impact: The ISO is attached to public GitHub releases (build-iso.yml:114-125). File mode 600 is meaningless inside a read-only squashfs that anyone can unsquashfs. The contained fine-grained PAT has Contents: Read/Write on the target repo, so an attacker can push arbitrary commits/results to the repository.
findings.recommendation: Never bake a long-lived write PAT into a public image. Upload results via a short-lived token, a GitHub App installation token minted at boot, or a dedicated results-only repository with minimum scope; otherwise ship the ISO with no upload credentials and have the operator drop bench-upload.conf on BENCHDATA. Document and test revocation of the baked PAT.

findings.title: Placeholder token 'change-me' is accepted silently; no token strength/startup validation
evidence: server/benchd.conf.example:6 - BENCHD_TOKEN=change-me
live/airootfs/etc/bench-agent.conf.example:11 - BENCHD_TOKEN=change-me
server/benchd.py:1413-1415 - find_token() returns any non-empty value from --token/$BENCHD_TOKEN/conf without validation
server/benchd.py:1430,1439-1441 - Handler.token is set to whatever was found; the only warning fires when the token is absent, not when it is a known placeholder
findings.impact: An operator copying the example verbatim gets a well-known, guessable operator token, and the server reports 'token+login' as if correctly configured. There is no length/entropy check, so a weak token is accepted without warning. There is also no runtime env validation for BENCHD_SERVER/token on the client side beyond a truthiness check (bench/agent.py:412-413).
findings.recommendation: Refuse to start (or hard-fail) when BENCHD_TOKEN is a known placeholder (change-me, changeme, test, empty) or is shorter than a minimum length; log a clear remediation. Add a unit test asserting weak tokens are rejected.

findings.title: No secret rotation / revocation / break-glass runbook or inventory
evidence: grep -ri 'rotat|revok|break.?glass|secret_rotation|emergency' across *.md returned only advisory sentences: README.md:162, README.md:362, AGENTS.md:181
docs/ contains CONTROL_PLANE.md, DATA.md, METHODOLOGY.md, FUTURE_WORK.md, PHASE_TIMINGS.md - no secret rotation runbook
Prompt 38 required companion artifacts secret_rotation_runbook.md, environment variable inventory, secret classification, emergency revocation plan - none present
findings.impact: The two tokens above (control-plane join/operator token, GitHub write PAT) have no documented rotation cadence, no revocation steps, and no evidence of ever being rotated. A leaked ISO/bundle token cannot be promptly revoked because the procedure is undocumented, and there is no inventory of which credentials exist or where they are baked.
findings.recommendation: Add docs/secret_rotation_runbook.md containing: an environment-variable/secret inventory, classification (operator token, runner key, GitHub PAT, OpenAI/LLM key if any), the exact rotation + revocation commands (request runner key re-issue; regenerate PAT; rebuild + re-release artifacts), a break-glass procedure, and a tested validation step. Track rotation dates/artifacts per the extended checks.

findings.title: Control-plane token exposed in URL query string and browser localStorage
evidence: server/benchd.py:15 - operators authenticate as bearer (API/CLI) or ?token= (web UI/SSE)
server/benchd.py:578-579 - query-string token is accepted for any endpoint
server/web/app.js:101 - TOKEN read from location.search ?token=
server/web/app.js:171 - token persisted to localStorage('benchd_token')
server/web/app.js:179,1582-1583 - EventSource and download links embed ?token=
server/benchd.py:518-524 - server log redacts token= (acknowledges the query-string risk)
findings.impact: A long-lived operator token placed in a URL leaks to browser history, Referer headers, bookmarks, and any reverse proxy that does not redact it, and it is readable by any same-origin JS via localStorage (the server also sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on every response - benchd.py:533).
findings.recommendation: Prefer a short-lived, HttpOnly session cookie established via a login POST, and use bearer headers for API calls. If query tokens are unavoidable for EventSource/downloads, mint separate short-TTL stream tokens scoped to read-only and avoid writing the operator token to persistent storage.

findings.title: Inconsistent token comparison and an unused BENCHD_INSECURE key
evidence: server/benchd.py:576 - bearer compared with secrets.compare_digest
server/benchd.py:578 - query-string token compared with '=='
server/benchd.py:586,598 - runner bearer compared with '=='
live/airootfs/usr/local/bin/bench-agent-env:42 - BENCHD_INSECURE is parsed/exported but no other file reads it (git grep found only this occurrence)
findings.impact: Mixed use of constant-time vs plain equality for token checks is an inconsistency; the practical timing risk is low but avoidable. BENCHD_INSECURE is advertised in the allowed-keys list yet is never consumed, so it silently does nothing - misleading operators about an insecure-TLS escape hatch.
findings.recommendation: Route every token comparison through secrets.compare_digest. Either implement BENCHD_INSECURE (with a loud warning) or remove it from the parser and docs to keep the naming/config set honest.

findings.title: Per-runner API key stored in cleartext; 0600 chmod is a no-op on Windows
evidence: bench/benchreport.py:341-342 - identity file ~/.config/bench-agent.json (or $BENCH_AGENT_IDENTITY)
bench/benchreport.py:355-374 - save_identity() writes {runner_id, api_key} as plain JSON, then os.chmod(p, 0o600) inside a try/except that swallows failures
server/benchd.py:1203,1217 - the server issues a per-runner api_key (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)) returned at registration
findings.impact: On Windows os.chmod cannot enforce POSIX mode bits, so the runner key sits in a user-profile file with default ACLs; the toolkit targets Windows PowerShell hosts. Any local process/user able to read the profile can impersonate the runner (and, because the token is also the join token path, is handed further privilege).
findings.recommendation: Document the credential file location/type in the secret inventory, set an owner-only ACL on Windows (icacls), and consider storing the runner key in the OS keyring. Add a test/check that the identity file is not group/world-readable on POSIX.
